title: Charts filled in at the end of the shift
topic: Raising concerns about systems and safety
stem:
You are an F2 doctor on an elderly care ward at 19:30. You notice two healthcare assistants completing the pressure-area care charts for several patients, filling in two-hourly turns for the whole day.

You have been on the ward most of the afternoon and didn't see some of those patients being turned. One of them, Mrs Lee, has a pressure ulcer.
instruction: Choose the 3 most appropriate actions to take in this situation.

options.text: Speak to the healthcare assistants privately about what you saw.
options.brief: Well meant, but the nurse in charge is better placed to address it.
options.detailed: A direct conversation can be appropriate, and they may have a reason, such as turns done but not recorded. But possible falsification of records, affecting patient care, needs the nurse in charge.

options.text: Make sure patients at high risk, including Mrs Lee, have their skin checked now.
options.brief: If turns were missed, these patients need checking.
options.detailed: Missed turns put frail patients at risk of new or worsening pressure damage. Checking their skin now deals with the immediate risk.

options.text: Leave it, as nursing documentation is a matter for the nursing team.
options.brief: It affects patient care, so it's your concern too.
options.detailed: Nursing records are the nursing team's responsibility, but you have seen something that may mean patients aren't receiving care.

options.text: Raise your concern with the nurse in charge.
options.brief: The nurse in charge can check what happened and address it.
options.detailed: The nurse in charge is responsible for the ward tonight and can find out whether turns were missed, and make sure care is given properly.

options.text: Report the healthcare assistants to the Nursing and Midwifery Council.
options.brief: HCAs aren't NMC registrants, and local routes come first.
options.detailed: Healthcare assistants aren't registered with the NMC, and concerns like this are first for the ward and trust to look into.

options.text: Report your concern through the incident reporting system.
options.brief: Records a possible pattern so it can be investigated.
options.detailed: Inaccurate charts and possibly missed care are a safety concern. Reporting it allows the ward manager and trust to look into it fairly.

options.text: Correct the charts yourself to show which turns you didn't see.
options.brief: You can't alter others' records, and you didn't see the whole day.
options.detailed: This may seem honest, but you can't change their records, and you weren't watching every patient all afternoon.

options.text: Ask the patients' relatives to keep an eye on whether they are turned.
options.detailed: Families may notice, but it isn't their role to monitor care, and this doesn't address the concern.

explanation.issue: This tests whether you act on a concern that records are being falsified and care missed, protecting patients first.
explanation.keyDetails: The charts were completed retrospectively. You didn't see some turns. One patient has a pressure ulcer. There may be an innocent explanation.
explanation.reasoning: [B] protects patients now, [D] involves the person responsible tonight, and [F] records the concern formally. The distractors handle it informally ([A]), ignore it or pass it to families ([C], [H]), escalate inappropriately ([E]), or alter records ([G]).
explanation.competing: [A] is the hard distractor: speaking to them directly can be appropriate, but possible falsification of records, with patients at risk, needs the nurse in charge.

references.title: Raising and acting on concerns about patient safety
references.note: Raising concerns about care and records.

references.title: Good medical practice
references.note: Domain 3, acting when patients may not be receiving the care they need.
